- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 74.25 → 76.67 in Example 2).
- Model underreacts to sustained downward trends; fails to mean-revert quickly after sharp declines (e.g., 68.16 → 64.92 in Example 1).
- Forecasts show lagged response to recent price movements; true values often turn sharply in the 10–15th day of the forecast horizon.
- Model exhibits “overconfidence” in short-term momentum, especially when history shows volatility; forecasts remain too high for 3–5 days after a spike.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model tends to overproject the trend into future days (e.g., 70.16 → 76.67 in Example 2).
- Model underestimates the impact of recent low prices; fails to recognize that prices may rebound from lows (e.g., 64.92 → 66.40 in Example 1).
- Forecasts are often too conservative in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, missing late-stage rebounds or corrections.
